questions.q: A car covers 150 km at a steady speed of 50 km/h. The time taken is
questions.e: Time = distance / speed = 150 / 50 = 3 hours.

questions.q: A man goes from his home to the office at 40 km/h and returns along the same road at 60 km/h. His average speed for the whole trip is
questions.e: Average = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h. The simple mean 50 is wrong for equal distances.

questions.q: A 120 m long train running at 54 km/h passes a signal pole in
questions.e: 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so time = 120 / 15 = 8 seconds.

questions.q: A 200 m long train crosses a 300 m long platform at a speed of 10 m/s. The time taken is
questions.e: Distance covered = 200 + 300 = 500 m, so time = 500 / 10 = 50 seconds.

questions.q: A boat goes 12 km/h in still water and the stream flows at 3 km/h. Its speed downstream is
questions.e: Downstream speed = 12 + 3 = 15 km/h. Upstream it would be 9 km/h.

questions.q: A boat covers 18 km in one hour downstream and 10 km in one hour upstream. The speed of the boat in still water is
questions.e: Still water speed = (18 + 10)/2 = 14 km/h. The stream is (18 − 10)/2 = 4 km/h.

questions.q: In a 1000 m race, A beats B by 100 m. When A reaches the finish, B has run
questions.e: A beats B by 100 m means B is 100 m behind the finish when A finishes, so B has run 900 m.

questions.q: A man walks at 5 km/h for 36 minutes. The distance he covers is
questions.e: 36 minutes = 0.6 hour, so distance = 5 × 0.6 = 3 km.

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 100 m run in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. They cross each other in
questions.e: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s and distance = 250 m, so time = 250 / 25 = 10 seconds.

questions.q: A 120 m train at 72 km/h overtakes an 80 m train running in the same direction at 54 km/h. The time taken to pass completely is
questions.e: Relative speed = 18 km/h = 5 m/s and distance = 200 m, so time = 200 / 5 = 40 seconds.

A cyclist rides 60 km at 30 km/h and the next 60 km at 60 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is
questions.e: Total time = 2 + 1 = 3 hours for 120 km, so average speed = 40 km/h. The simple mean 45 is wrong.

questions.q: A 120 m long train passes a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 seconds. The speed of the train is
questions.e: Relative speed = 120/12 = 10 m/s = 36 km/h. Train speed = 36 + 6 = 42 km/h.

questions.q: A man reaches his destination 10 minutes late at 40 km/h and 5 minutes early at 50 km/h. The distance is
questions.e: The time difference is 15 min = ¼ hour, so d/40 − d/50 = ¼. This gives d/200 = ¼ and d = 50 km.

questions.q: Town P and town Q are 280 km apart. A car leaves P at 8 am towards Q at 40 km/h, and another car leaves Q at 9 am towards P at 60 km/h. They meet at
questions.e: By 9 am the first car has covered 40 km, leaving 240 km. They close at 100 km/h, so they meet 2.4 hours (2 h 24 min) after 9 am, at 11:24 am.

questions.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations X and Y towards each other. After meeting, the first takes 9 hours and the second takes 4 hours to reach the destinations. The ratio of the speeds of the first to the second is
questions.e: Speed ratio = √(time taken by second : time taken by first) = √(4 : 9) = 2 : 3.

questions.q: A boat takes three times as long to cover a distance upstream as downstream. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, the speed of the boat in still water is
questions.e: Time ratio 3 : 1 means (b + 4) = 3(b − 4), so b + 4 = 3b − 12 and b = 8 km/h.

questions.q: In a 1000 m race, A beats B by 100 m or by 10 seconds. A's time for the race is
questions.e: B covers 100 m in 10 s, so B's speed is 10 m/s and B takes 100 s. A takes 10 s less, which is 90 s.

questions.q: A 150 m long train crosses a signal pole in 10 seconds and a platform in 25 seconds. The length of the platform is
questions.e: Speed = 150/10 = 15 m/s. In 25 s it covers 375 m, which is train plus platform, so platform = 375 − 150 = 225 m.
